user_question: Compare the top 3 open-source vector databases for a startup building RAG products
short_answer: For a startup focused on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), the three most relevant open-source vector databases are Milvus, Qdrant, and Weaviate. Milvus excels at high-volume, large-scale workloads with multiple index types and strong filtering, Qdrant offers a lightweight, Rust-based engine with fast HNSW search and real-time performance, and Weaviate provides built-in hybrid search (vector + BM25), extensive LLM integration modules, and a custom HNSW index that is well-suited for RAG pipelines.

key_findings.claim: Milvus is an open-source vector database that supports multiple ANN index types (HNSW, IVF, and disk-based) and is designed for high-volume vector retrieval workloads, offering filtering and scaling primitives.
Milvus handles write-heavy patterns with streaming indexing and background compaction, helping maintain query latency above 10 million vectors.
Qdrant is a high-performance, open-source vector database written in Rust that uses HNSW indexing and is faster than PGVector in some large-corpus benchmarks.
Qdrant is designed for real-time applications and offers fast throughput for large datasets, although the available evidence does not detail its hybrid search or filtering capabilities.
Weaviate is an open-source, AI-native vector database that implements a custom HNSW index and provides built-in hybrid search combining vector similarity with BM25 keyword search.
Weaviate offers modules for vectorization, reranking, and generative workflows, making it integrated with LLM-based RAG pipelines.
Weaviate's hybrid search and enterprise features, including filtering, security, and scalability, are highlighted as strengths for RAG use cases.

limitations_or_assumptions: The evidence does not provide direct side-by-side performance benchmarks or cost comparisons for the three databases.
Information on filtering strength, hybrid search, and integration depth is limited for Qdrant.
There is no data on deployment complexity, community activity, or long-term support for each project.
The comparison assumes that the startup's RAG workload requires high-volume vector retrieval and hybrid search capabilities.
The GitHub repository lookup did not provide usable results for Weaviate.
suggested_next_steps: Run a benchmark with your own embedding dimensions, vector count, and query patterns on Milvus, Qdrant, and Weaviate to measure latency, throughput, and recall.
Evaluate integration with your existing LLM stack and the availability of pre-built vectorization and reranking modules.
Assess community support, documentation quality, and release cadence for each project.
Consider hybrid search requirements when selecting between the databases.
If real-time performance and lightweight deployment are critical, test Qdrant in a production-like environment.
